title: Polygon Party
body:
Goal: draw three shapes in a row, each with its own for loop: a triangle, a square and a hexagon.

  1. Open starter.py. The triangle is already done - read its loop.
  2. Write a loop for the square (4 sides, turn 360 / 4 = ?).
  3. Write a loop for the hexagon (6 sides, turn 360 / 6 = ?). Sides of 60 fit nicely on the screen.
  4. Press Run (F5) after each shape.

Done looks like: an orange triangle, a sky-blue square and a green hexagon, all closed.

Extra: add a fourth shape below the others (try t.goto(-50, -200)): an octagon (8 sides) in purple "#CC79A7".

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Read the triangle loop at the top of starter.py. It already works. The square and the hexagon need a loop that looks just like it, with different numbers.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: In a for loop, range(...) says how many sides to draw. Inside the loop, t.forward(...) draws a side and t.left(...) turns. The turn is always 360 divided by the number of sides.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Under each # TODO, write a loop like this: for i in range(____):. Push the next two lines in by 4 spaces: t.forward(____) and t.left(____). Use the side lengths from the comments. Work out each turn with 360 divided by the sides.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Polygon Party
# Every shape gets its own loop. The turn is always 360 / number of sides.

import turtle

t = turtle.Turtle()
t.shape("turtle")
t.pensize(3)

# Shape 1: a triangle (3 sides, turn 360 / 3 = 120)
t.penup()          # lift the pen: move without drawing
t.goto(-250, 0)
t.pendown()        # put the pen back down
t.color("#E69F00")
for i in range(3):
    t.forward(100)
    t.left(120)

# Shape 2: a square (4 sides, turn 360 / 4 = ?)
t.penup()
t.goto(-50, 0)
t.pendown()
t.color("#56B4E9")
# TODO: write a loop that draws a square with sides of 100

# Shape 3: a hexagon (6 sides, turn 360 / 6 = ?)
t.penup()
t.goto(150, 0)
t.pendown()
t.color("#009E73")
# TODO: write a loop that draws a hexagon with sides of 60

turtle.done()
